title: Rewrite textureProjLod usage to avoid a Vulkan validation error.
body:
Fixes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/98390.

This PR may introduce some visual changes although I haven't spotted them yet. I'll give the background behind the error and what I spotted along the way when studying the code involved.

The problem is the usage of shadow samplers with a texture that is not a depth texture. This is stated to be undefined behavior. There's two possible solutions to the problem: we copy the contents of the shadow texture to a depth texture (which costs as much as one full texture blit), or we modify the sampling to do the depth comparison manually. This PR implements the second solution.

However, upon diving into the code that makes use of this, there's a few things worth noting:
- We have code that does "Nearest", PCF5 or PCF13 manually by gathering samplers _horizontally_ on the texture, as it seems the information is encoded in a single row.
- The sampler that is used for this operation isn't configured to use nearest filtering however, but linear. Which means the sampler is allowed to do taps vertically, which is probably not intended, as it seems everything for a particular light is only encoded in one row.
- The context of how this code does filtering manually and calls it "Nearest" explicitly leads me to believe an assumption was made that the sampler at the low level does behave like nearest, which isn't the case at the moment.
- It seems the most reasonable solution is to turn the shadow sampler to Nearest, which avoids the need to do extra samples that go unused, especially the vertical ones.

It is possible a small performance regression is expected, but it doesn't seem like there's a way around that to fix the validation error, and this is probably less harmful than doing a full texture copy.

My reference for replicating the function is this: https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/textureProjLod.xhtml
> textureProjLod performs a texture lookup with projection from an explicitly specified level-of-detail. The texture coordinates consumed from P, not including the last component of P, are divided by the last component of P. The resulting 3rd component of P in the shadow forms is used as Dref. After these values are computed, the texture lookup proceeds as in textureLod, with lod used to specify the level-of-detail from which the texture will be sampled.
